sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fast-Casual Self-Serve Broth Bowl Master Licensing

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Common Law statutory corporate framework with customary law elements)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Compact of Free Association between the Government of the United States and the Government of the Republic of the Marshall Islands (1986, as amended 2003) - investment-related provisions and trade preferences; not a standalone bilateral investment treaty
No comprehensive double-taxation agreement or bilateral investment treaty is currently in force exclusively for the RMI non-resident tax-exempt corporate regime.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: RMI Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2012, as amended (AMLCFTA); AML/CFT Financial Integrity Regulations 2013, as amended; Business Corporations Act 1990 (RMI BCA), as amended; Beneficial Ownership Regulations 2020 (confidential Government-access beneficial ownership filing regime).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of full passport of each proposed director, shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office / local Notary Public in document origin country

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement) of each UBO/director, not older than 3 months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank; notarized by local Notary Public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and/or good-standing certificate from the principal banking institution for each UBO/director
Franchisor corporate registration certificate and business license (PRC State Administration for Market Regulation) for the Chinese master licensor and its UBO chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation, People's Republic of China; notarized by PRC Notary Public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing of any intermediate holding entity in the ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the holding entity's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, signatories and beneficial owners against OFAC SDN/SSI lists, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, UK HMT sanctions, and RMI domestic designations. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are identified under FATF 12-month standard; enhanced due diligence, source of wealth/source of funds evidence, and senior-management approval are required. Negative news searches and adverse media checks are mandatory. Screening documentation must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations Online Filing and Name-Clearance Portal (administered by the Office of the Registrar of Corporations, Ministry of Finance, Majuro; generally accessed through a licensed registered agent)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be in English/Latin script. A Chinese-character name cannot be registered as the legal corporate name. The Chinese trading name must be transliterated into pinyin and presented with an English translation on the name-clearance application; a non-Latin secondary name may be noted only as an alternate registered name in the register.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, banking, trust, insurance, assurance, reinsurance, securities, investment, fund, fiduciary - require a separate financial-services license from the Banking Commissioner/Insurance Commissioner before name clearance can be issued
Government, national, republic, federal, state, commonwealth, municipality, official - implies governmental patronage and is refused absent ministerial consent
University, college, institute, academy - requires evidence of educational accreditation
Chamber of commerce, solicitor, attorney, legal, law, doctor, clinic, medical - requires registration with the relevant professional body
NGO, charity, foundation, cooperative - may trigger NGO registration and beneficial ownership transparency rules
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Registrar of Corporations within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice. The appeal must set out the corrected name or evidence of entitlement to the sensitive token. The Registrar must decide within 10 business days. A further ministerial review may be filed with the Ministry of Finance within 14 calendar days of the second refusal. There is no additional statutory fee for an administrative appeal, but the applicant must submit a new name reservation request and the standard government fee if any name amendment becomes necessary.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not acceptable for the statutory registered office. The BC must maintain a physical registered office at the address of a licensed RMI registered agent. For a non-resident food-franchise licensing company, no operating premises or local staff in the Marshall Islands are required, and business operations and trademark-licensing activity may be conducted wholly overseas.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; quantified at less than 5% annually for a non-resident BC with no in-jurisdiction operations, but the Registrar and the Financial Intelligence Unit retain statutory power to require physical inspection of the registered agent's records, including UBO files.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; fixed fee per corporate entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; fixed legal opinion fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act, 1990 (BCA), codified as Title 39 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code (MIRC); § 44 (execution and filing of Articles of Incorporation), § 43 (consideration for shares), § 48 (initial directors), § 60 (registered office and registered agent), § 66 (action by directors without meeting), § 117 (annual government fee and reporting), § 75 (replacement share certificates)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands (all submissions routed through an AMIRA-licensed registered agent)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital requirement. The BCA permits authorized capital of one or more shares with or without par value and leaves subscription consideration to the incorporator's discretion. As a non-resident domestic corporation, no escrow of capital or proof of payment is required at incorporation; paid-in capital is recorded in the subscription agreement, share register, and corporate books.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the incorporator of [CORPORATION NAME], a Marshall Islands Business Corporation, adopts this First Board Resolution. The Board accepts the subscription of [SUBSCRIBER] for 1,000 common shares, no par value, valued at US$1.00 per share, pursuant to BCA § 43. The Board adopts the registered office address of [REGISTERED AGENT], Majuro, Marshall Islands, and appoints said agent as registered agent under BCA § 60. The Board appoints [NAME] as President, [NAME] as Secretary, and [NAME] as Treasurer, each to hold office until the next annual meeting. The Board authorizes execution of banking resolutions, opening of bank accounts, and filing of all statutory documents, and directs the Secretary to record this resolution in the corporate minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Registered Agent Engagement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations (acting through an AMIRA-licensed registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request to the Registrar through a licensed AMIRA registered agent, screening the proposed corporate name against the active registry to ensure no conflict or misleading similarity. Simultaneously execute a registered agent service agreement designating the physical registered office in Majuro and confirm the agent's written consent to act.
required_dossiers: Registered agent acceptance letter and service agreement
Due diligence/KYC questionnaire for each ultimate beneficial owner
Certified copy of passport for each incorporator and initial director
Proof of residential address for officers, directors, and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or conflicts with an existing registration, file an amended request with up to two alternate names or submit a notarized consent from the conflicting entity; the Registrar issues a clearance within 1 business day after the corrected submission, and the initial reservation period is extended accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public and AMIRA-licensed Registered Agent (drafting); Registrar of Corporations (substantive review)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name, registered office and agent in Majuro, authorized share structure (e.g., 1,000 common shares, no par value), a broad purpose clause authorizing master franchise licensing and brand management for the ISIC 5610 fast-casual broth-bowl concept, an indemnification provision, and the name of the initial director. The incorporator signs the Articles before a notary public, and the registered agent countersigns the consent to act.
required_dossiers: Written action of incorporator appointing initial directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a deficiency query, the registered agent files a corrective statement under BCA § 44(5) within 7 calendar days clarifying the share class, purpose clause, or director appointment; the deficiency hold does not invalidate the name reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Articles of Incorporation, together with the US$150 government filing fee and the registered agent's certified consent, either in person at the Office of the Attorney General or via the registered agent's electronic filing portal. Upon substantive review, the Registrar endorses the Articles and issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the official registration number and seal.
required_dossiers: Registered agent consent and Majuro office address confirmation
Cover letter of the AMIRA-licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected for a substantive defect, the agent resubmits a corrected Articles filing within 14 days; expedited same-day refiling is available for an additional US$100 expedite fee, and the certificate date will reflect the original submission if a curative statement is accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold an organizational meeting, or execute an unanimous written consent in lieu of meeting under BCA § 66(2), at which the First Board Resolution is adopted. The Board approves the subscription of shares, adopts the registered office and agent, appoints the initial officers (President, Secretary, Treasurer), approves the corporate seal, and authorizes management to open bank accounts and to negotiate master franchise and royalty agreements.
required_dossiers: Waiver of notice of organizational meeting
First Board Resolution (pro-forma text as approved)
Bank account resolution and authorized signatory list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a quorum defect or director dissent appears, the corporation executes an unanimous written consent in lieu of meeting stating the effective date; a corrected resolution supersedes the defective minutes and is filed in the corporate record book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Shares, Corporate Kit, and Registered Office Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Issue the definitive share certificate or certificates to the subscriber against receipt of the agreed subscription price, enter the subscriber's name in the statutory share register, and open the registered office register maintained at the registered agent's Majuro address. Deliver the corporate kit containing the corporate seal, share certificate book, minute book, and stock transfer ledger to the client.
required_dossiers: Share certificate No. 1 issued to subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a share certificate is lost, destroyed, or defective, the Board may authorize issuance of a replacement certificate against an indemnity bond in accordance with BCA § 75; the registered agent records the cancellation and reissue in the share register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax-Exempt Status Confirmation and Annual Compliance Calendar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Marshall Islands Ministry of Finance (Revenue Division) and Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the non-resident domestic corporation status for tax-exemption purposes such that no income tax, withholding tax, or capital gains tax is levied on foreign-source income under applicable Marshall Islands tax law. Register for the annual registry franchise fee and file the annual confirmation return with the Registrar by the anniversary date of incorporation to maintain good standing and to permit issuance of a Certificate of Good Standing for banking and royalty-wire counterparties.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Good Standing (requested upon filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is filed late, a reinstatement application under BCA § 117(4) with the applicable late fee and penalty is submitted within 6 months of the anniversary date; delayed filing beyond six months may trigger administrative dissolution, which is cured only by a formal reinstatement order from the Registrar.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Marshall Islands Ministry of Finance, Business License Division (for any in-country commercial presence); Marshall Islands Visitors Authority (food-service brand certification); Registrar of Corporations (annual registry license for the non-resident BC master franchisor)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business License under the Business License Act 1989 for local operations, or Foreign Investment Business License (FIBL) if a foreign-owned operating subsidiary is later established within the Republic. For the non-resident master licensing vehicle, the only recurring license obligation is the annual registry franchise license under BCA § 117 together with a maintained Certificate of Good Standing; no premises-based operating license is required for a purely administrative and intellectual-property licensing presence.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Authority (RMI EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for the non-resident BC because the entity operates no physical premises, industrial discharge points, or emissions within the Republic; the RMI EPA exemption applies under Section 8(4) of the Environmental Protection Act 1984 for purely administrative and registered-office activities. Any downstream in-country restaurant licensee engaged in ISIC 5610 food preparation must obtain a Registration-tier EIA clearance, escalating to a Full EIA Report if projected wastewater, cooking-oil, or VOC emissions exceed RMI EPA thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Contractual pass-through standards imposed on all downstream franchise licensees: kitchen VOC exhaust not exceeding 600 ppm; wastewater effluent with BOD5 no greater than 50 mg/L and COD no greater than 250 mg/L; grease-trap waste documented under RMI EPA solid waste manifest rules; segregated solid waste hauled by licensed contractors; and bulk cooking-oil storage confined to compliant double-wall tanks. The master franchise agreement requires each licensee to hold all applicable RMI EPA permits and discharge authorizations before commencing operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification: annual fire safety inspection and certificate from the Majuro Fire Department for the registered-office suite; for any downstream in-country restaurant, building fire clearance, automatic kitchen hood suppression system inspection, exit-route plan approval, and food-hall electrical load certification. Occupational clearance: workplace registration with the RMI Occupational Health and Safety Division, hazard communication training records for all staff handling food-contact surfaces and cleaning chemicals, and emergency preparedness signage as required for commercial food service premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Revenue and Taxation Division, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands — official government tax portal: rmi.gov.mh. Customs and import/export duties are independently administered by the Marshall Islands Customs Service.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Appoint an RMI-licensed registered agent; file Articles of Incorporation under the Business Corporation Act 1990; obtain the Company Registration Number from the Registrar of Corporations; file the annual Economic Statement confirming non-resident status. No separate VAT or income-tax registration certificate is issued because non-resident domestic corporations are statutorily exempt and no VAT regime exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The Business Corporation Act Section 103 election automatically classifies a non-resident domestic corporation as tax-exempt where all business activity occurs outside the RMI and no domestic property or income is present. RMI law provides no check-the-box election, hybrid-mismatch election, or IRS-style entity classification mechanism for this foreign-owned Business Corporation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No national VAT or GST is imposed. Indirect taxation consists solely of territorial customs duties under the Customs and Tariff Act 1990 (import duty, fuel tax, and visitor green tax); no federal, state, or municipal sales/use tax exists in the Marshall Islands.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — the RMI imposes no VAT/GST registration threshold. Import duty registration (Customs Importer Number) applies to every commercial consignment regardless of turnover. The official currency of the RMI is the United States Dollar (USD).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No e-invoicing mandate, real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government API schema exists for business-to-business invoices. Import/export declaration data is submitted exclusively through the ASYCUDA World electronic customs clearance platform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: No export VAT zero-rating mechanism applies because the RMI levies no VAT/GST; physical exports are duty-exempt and there is no VAT refund claim system. For the fast-casual Chinese Malatang self-serve licensing model, royalty and franchise fee income is RMI-exempt where the licensed IP is exploited solely outside the RMI and remittances are received outside RMI tax jurisdiction, making a refund claim unnecessary.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Master Franchise and License Agreement executed under RMI Business Corporation law with the Chinese-Malatang sub-licensee
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/TT/ACH credit advice evidencing royalty receipt for the licensed franchise territory
Annual Economic Statement filed with the RMI Registrar of Corporations demonstrating no RMI-sourced activity
Board minutes and director resolutions confirming offshore governance and non-resident decision-making
AML/KYC records of the receiving bank and source-of-funds documentation for the royalty remittance
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: A false Section 103 exemption filing subjects the corporation to a fine of up to USD 5,000, revocation of exempt status, and retrospective income tax assessment under the Income Tax Act 1989 with statutory penalty and interest. Customs misdeclaration entails seizure, forfeiture, a fine up to USD 10,000, and imprisonment up to five years under the Customs and Tariff Act 1990. No VAT clawback exists because there is no VAT regime.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banking Commissioner, Republic of the Marshall Islands (regulatory authority within the Ministry of Finance; no central bank is established)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The United States dollar is the sole legal tender of the Marshall Islands. There are no foreign exchange controls, and both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible. Profit, royalty, and dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders or franchisors are unrestricted, subject only to standard anti-money-laundering record-keeping, sanctions screening, and prudent banking due-diligence requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion regime exists in the Marshall Islands. Export receipts and royalty proceeds may be retained in USD, held in any eligible account, and disbursed without any mandated conversion ratio or repatriation timeline.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. The Marshall Islands has no dedicated e-money licensing regime, and the Banking Commissioner does not recognize offshore digital EMIs as eligible clearing agents for core depository or royalty collection accounts. Such EMIs may be used only for ancillary low-value collections, subject to RMI licensing, sanctions compliance, and express bank-form approval; they cannot replace a licensed RMI commercial bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical presence or in-person interview at a licensed RMI commercial bank branch is effectively mandatory for non-resident corporations. Remote account opening is not generally permitted. The Banking Commissioner expects authorized signatories, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners to appear in person at the Majuro branch or to complete a bank-approved notarized and apostilled certification process with exceptional cause.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident business corporation with no physical RMI office or employees
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Good Standing, registered agent letter, articles of incorporation, corporate bylaws, board resolutions, beneficial ownership schedule, notarized passports and proof of residence for all directors, shareholder register and source-of-funds evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border royalty and franchise-fee inflows to a non-resident franchisor entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Franchise agreements, trademark license registrations, royalty calculation reports, audited or internally reviewed financial statements, sample remittance invoices, beneficial ownership details of franchisees, and jurisdictional tax compliance attestations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-heavy self-serve restaurant collections being remitted as royalties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: POS settlement statements, daily sales and transaction logs, reconciliation reports, store-level tax filings, franchise operations manual showing cash-control procedures, and bank flow diagrams demonstrating conversion of POS receipts into lawful royalty wires.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections from shareholders must be executed in USD via SWIFT MT103 to the RMI bank's U.S. correspondent account, with payment narrative referencing the entity name, 'Capital Contribution' purpose code, and the applicable board resolution or subscription agreement. The RMI bank and its U.S. correspondent require a funds-transfer originator statement, beneficial ownership attestation, and documentary link to the share allotment. Retained intercompany loans or non-equity pass-through funds are not acceptable as capital and must be documented as debt, with appropriate loan agreements and interest terms.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outward supplier and trade settlement payments should be cleared through SWIFT MT103 for vendor invoices and royalty disbursements, or MT202 for interbank transfers where no beneficiary account detail is available. Large equipment purchases and franchise build-out imports may be routed through irrevocable commercial letters of credit issued by the RMI bank and advised via a U.S. or Singapore correspondent bank, with invoices, bills of lading, and inspection certificates attached. Documentary collections are permitted but are less suited for fast-casual franchise supply chains.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of the Business Corporation (Business Corporations Act 1990, as amended, Section 110)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Marshall Islands Corporate Registry (Office of the Attorney General)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: file on or before the last day of the month containing the anniversary of incorporation, each year, submitted through the licensed Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Minimum USD 250 late penalty assessed by the Registrar after the due date; two consecutive years of non-filing expose the corporation to administrative dissolution/strike-off and loss of good standing status

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation Record (AML/KYC refresh submitted through the licensed Registered Agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Registered Agent; confidential beneficial ownership register maintained by the Registrar of Corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the Annual Report and immediately upon any transfer, issue, or other change in shareholding or controlling ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or stale UBO records render the corporation non-compliant with AML/KYC regulations, may trigger a monetary penalty on the Registered Agent, and may be cited in strike-off proceedings for persistent non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit for a non-resident Business Corporation. An audit becomes compulsory only where the corporation is (i) listed or seeking listing on a recognized stock exchange, (ii) engaged in banking, insurance, or other regulated financial activity, or (iii) expressly ordered by the Registrar following a shareholder petition or formal investigation
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for all financial statements prepared voluntarily or under contractual obligations; the Business Corporations Act requires correct and complete books of account but does not mandate preparation of local GAAP financial statements for non-resident corporations

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic does not maintain a public beneficial ownership register. The licensed Registered Agent must hold current beneficial ownership records revealing any natural person holding or controlling more than 25% of issued shares, with the full control chain; an annual confirmation is executed on each incorporation anniversary, and an interim confirmation is required at every share transfer or change of control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable by statute; voluntary certified IFRS audit USD 3,500 - USD 7,500

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% - the Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) imposes no corporate income tax on non-resident domestic business corporations.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective rate; no statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions are necessary because the tax base is nil. Royalties, management fees, dividends, and capital gains flowing through the RMI Business Corporation are not subject to RMI income tax. Annual registration and business license fees are regulatory charges, not income taxes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: None. RMI prescribes no corporate income tax return and operates no income tax e-filing portal. Non-tax annual compliance is conducted through the RMI Corporate Registry by a licensed registered agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Not applicable for income tax; annual registry renewal is the only recurring filing obligation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No statutory income tax filing deadline applies. Annual corporate registry renewal is due on the anniversary or license renewal cycle; late renewal attracts late fees and possible strike-off.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: There are no RMI income tax boxes or schedules to complete. A non-resident Business Corporation has no taxable income, deduction, credit, or loss computation in RMI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident BC should not file an RMI income tax return. It should maintain corporate records, board resolutions, share register, IP ownership documentation, franchise agreements, and bank statements to evidence non-resident status and commercial substance if required by foreign tax or licensing authorities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: No late filing penalty applies because no income tax return is due. Failure to pay annual registry or business license fees can lead to administrative penalties, loss of good standing, and strike-off; reinstatement requires payment of arrears and late fees through the registered agent.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - RMI imposes no dividend withholding tax on distributions to shareholders, resident or non-resident.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: RMI has no comprehensive double taxation treaty network and does not require a tax residency certificate for domestic withholding relief because no RMI withholding is imposed. For foreign-source withholding, the RMI BC cannot rely on an RMI treaty absent a specific treaty. If a foreign market requires documentary proof, the BC may obtain a certificate of good standing from the RMI Registrar; that certificate is not a tax residency certificate and does not by itself create treaty relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: RMI statutory rate: 0% on outgoing royalties and interest. In foreign source jurisdictions, e.g., the People's Republic of China (PRC), outbound royalties and interest paid to an RMI non-resident BC generally attract PRC domestic withholding tax of 10% each in the absence of an applicable tax treaty. If a PRC permanent establishment exists, net-basis taxation and branch profit repatriation rules may apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 0 - no RMI transfer-pricing documentation threshold exists. For cross-border operations in an enforcing source country, contemporaneous TP documentation may be required under local rules; e.g., PRC thresholds commonly include RMB 100 million for related-party intangible or royalty flows, RMB 200 million for tangible property transfers, and RMB 400 million for aggregate other related-party transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: RMI Economic Substance Regulations apply to RMI tax-resident entities carrying on relevant activities. The franchise master-licensing model is within the holding-company and IP-related activity class. A non-resident BC must be able to demonstrate genuine economic substance in its operating market, including actual board decisions, IP development, franchise oversight, local staff, business premises, and commercial records. False ESR declarations, nominee shell arrangements, and wholly passive royalty collection create ESR and foreign anti-avoidance exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Concealment of Foreign Business Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the RMI BC to conceal taxable restaurant or franchise profits in a source jurisdiction, understating local POS cash sales, or routing cash through shell accounts before paying royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RMI itself asserts no income tax on the BC. The source jurisdiction may reassess tax, impose a daily late surcharge, assess a civil penalty of 0.5 to 5 times the tax evaded, and refer the matter for criminal tax prosecution when thresholds are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced on grounds of fraud or sham. Directors and shareholders can be held jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax, interest, civil restitution, criminal fines, and imprisonment; exit bans or travel restrictions may be imposed during a cross-border tax investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Royalty Drain and Transfer Pricing Adjustment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Characterising operating profits as 'royalties' paid to the RMI BC without genuine IP ownership, without legally enforceable franchise agreements, or at non-arm's-length rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The source country may recharacterise the payments, disallow tax deductions, impose withholding tax on the adjusted payment, and assess interest and penalties. General anti-abuse rules may treat the RMI BC as sham or tax resident where management and control actually occur.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute artificial royalty agreements or falsify IP documentation may be joined in tax adjustment proceedings; fraudulent conduct removes limited-liability protection and exposes directors to personal liability and criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The RMI BC has no office, employees, IP development activity, or meaningful board oversight, while receiving substantial royalty income and presenting itself as the master franchisor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RMI may impose ESR penalties, suspend the license, or strike the company off the register. Foreign jurisdictions may apply CFC, subpart F, GILTI, or anti-hybrid rules and impute income to shareholders; the RMI BC may be re-domiciled for tax purposes into the market of operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal liability for contracts entered into after strike-off. Nominee directors who sign false ESR declarations face fines, disqualification, and criminal liability; registered agents may cease services, accelerating insolvency and enforcement risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and AML Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mixing Local POS cash receipts with royalty wires through the RMI BC without proper KYC, beneficial ownership disclosure, or legitimate underlying franchise contracts, and layering funds through multiple accounts or jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RMI anti-money laundering legislation imposes criminal forfeiture, substantial fines, and imprisonment for laundering criminal proceeds. Banks may freeze accounts, file suspicious activity reports, and terminate banking relationships; the BC may lose good standing for AML compliance failure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who direct suspicious wire transfers, sign false beneficial ownership returns, or fail to maintain AML/KYC records are personally liable. Interim measures may include asset freezing, travel bans, passport surrender, and criminal prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling Chinese malatang self-serve master licences before satisfying local franchise registration, trademark recordal, food-safety licensing, and foreign-investment or business-license requirements in both RMI and the source market.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Local franchise regulators may issue fines, stop-orders, compensation awards to franchisees, and license revocation; unregistered trademark licensing may render the underlying IP unenforceable and expose the franchisor to injunctions and damages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who personally approve or market unregistered franchise packages may be liable in tort for fraudulent misrepresentation, ordered to pay restitution, disqualified as directors, and subjected to monetary or criminal penalties in the operating jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File Annual Registry, ESR, and Beneficial Ownership Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing RMI annual corporate registry renewal, ESR nil-return obligations, or beneficial ownership declarations while continuing to receive royalty and franchise fee payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing penalties and administrative suspension accrue; persistent non-compliance leads to automatic strike-off, loss of legal personality, and inability to enforce franchise agreements or hold bank accounts in the company's name.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorise trading after strike-off are personally liable for debts incurred during the unauthorised period. Reinstatement is discretionary and requires payment of arrears, penalties, and proof of ongoing good standing.
